findings.severity_note: repair by making admission_pass_history() (or the instrument's caller) read the day-partitioned log through read_pass_verdicts, in a node holding reckon/crew/runs.py and scripts/measure_queue_drain.py.
findings.text: the seven-day read is called by nothing in production: read_pass_verdicts has no caller outside tests/test_the_verdict_log_covers_a_week.py, and scripts/measure_queue_drain.py:146 still builds measure_drain from runs_module.admission_pass_history(), which reads the single current file, so the drain instrument a real drain runs still reports the sliver §47 exists to remove. Repair by feeding read_pass_verdicts()['records'] into measure_drain's passes, which needs write scope in reckon/crew/runs.py and scripts/measure_queue_drain.py, neither of which this node was fenced to.

findings.severity_note: repair by pointing the three readers at read_pass_verdicts' file set (or at _pass_record_paths) in the same node that wires the instrument.
findings.text: admission_pass_history() reads only crew_home()/admission-verdicts.jsonl, and obligations.py:2279 admission_verdicts() and obligations.py:2309 recent_upstream_retirements() read the same single file. The rotation this change lands moves every record of a completed day into a separate day file at the first append of the next day, so after midnight these three readers see only the current day: a retirement recorded yesterday, and the pass history a stuck verdict counts across, vanish from them. The node updated its own _last_verdict_of/_last_stage_seconds for exactly this and left these readers on the current file.

findings.severity_note: repair by extending _append_crew_log_line with the home parameter, or by calling it for the append and keeping only rotation/pruning local.
findings.text: verdict_log_append re-implements reckon/crew/picker/__init__.py:83 _append_crew_log_line -- crew-home mkdir, json.dumps(separators=(',',':'), default=str), one os.write on an O_APPEND descriptor, and a swallowed failure -- instead of calling it, and the diff removes the call to that owner the base revision already made. The only capability the addition has that the owner lacks is a caller-supplied home for tests; the rotation and prune around the append do not require the append itself to be re-written.

findings.severity_note: repair by asserting the reported per-day figure against an independently computed byte count from the fixture files, or by dropping the line and resting the cost claim on the ceiling check.
findings.text: assert abs(cost['one_copy_bytes_per_day'] - PASSES_PER_DAY * mean_row) < 1.0 compares a value the test computed from its own inputs with those same inputs: measure_verdict_log_cost returns one_copy_bytes_per_day = round(verdicts_per_day * mean_row_bytes, 1) and the test passes exactly PASSES_PER_DAY and mean_row, so the two sides move together and the line reddens only if round() breaks. It cannot fail on any regression in the rotation, the read, or the cost accounting it was added for.

findings.severity_note: repair by writing fixture rows at the live row size for a day's live pass count, so the ceiling is the realised cost of one simulated live day.
findings.text: assert max(read['bytes_per_day'].values()) <= live_ceiling compares the fixture's day files (~24 KB each, twelve 2 KB rows) against a ceiling of 2 x 1,065.1 x 19,259.6 = about 41 MB, so the assertion holds with a factor of roughly 1,700 to spare and would pass if a day file grew a thousandfold. The done_when asks the byte cost to be bounded by the live-log rate and row size; the two live figures are recorded as constants but the fixture reproduces neither, so this line measures the fixture's arithmetic, not the retained log's cost.
